title: Global Legal Discovery Optimization
business: International law firms managing massive multilingual document repositories for cross-border litigation.
problem: Traditional keyword-based search fails to identify semantically related evidence across different languages, leading to missed critical documents and increased manual review costs.
solution: By utilizing text-embedding-3-large, firms can convert multilingual legal documents into high-dimensional numerical vectors. This allows the system to measure the relatedness between documents regardless of the source language, enabling semantic retrieval that surfaces relevant evidence based on conceptual meaning rather than exact keyword matching.
steps: Pre-process raw legal documents by cleaning and normalizing text across various languages.
Send the processed text to the v1/embeddings endpoint specifying text-embedding-3-large to generate vector representations.
Store the resulting high-dimensional vectors in a specialized vector database for efficient similarity search.
Execute semantic queries by embedding search terms and performing nearest-neighbor lookups against the stored document vectors.
outcome: Legal teams experience a significant improvement in discovery precision, as the system surfaces conceptually relevant documents that would have been ignored by standard keyword searches.
limitation: The model produces high-dimensional vectors that require significant storage and computational resources for similarity calculations; developers should monitor latency during large-scale retrieval operations to ensure performance remains within acceptable bounds.

import openai
# Generate embedding for a legal document
response = openai.Embedding.create(
    input="Evidence text here",
    model="text-embedding-3-large" # Specifies the most capable model
)
vector = response['data'][0]['embedding']
